long_biography.plain_text:
Rosso began experimenting with clothing as a teenager, using a family sewing machine to make jeans before studying textile manufacturing. He later joined Adriano Goldschmied's business and helped create Diesel in 1978. Seven years later, he bought his partner's interest and gained sole control, giving him the equity base from which the denim label became an international premium brand.

He created OTB as a holding company for Diesel and subsequent fashion investments, adding production businesses and houses including Maison Margiela, Marni, Viktor&Rolf and Jil Sander. Rosso remains founder and chairman, responsible for strategic direction, while a separate chief executive administers the group day to day. Fashion therefore remains both the source and principal current sector of his wealth. His private investment company, Red Circle Investments, has expanded into technology, food, health, funds, property and hospitality, but none displaces OTB as the dominant disclosed platform. Rosso's founder interest is personal economic ownership; OTB's turnover, stores, trademarks, debt and portfolio-brand valuations belong to the company and cannot be treated as his personal assets.
